links.outcome: Baseline reading grade level of OrthoInfo spine patient education articles versus AMA sixth-grade target
links.effect: Mean Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level 9.5 (SD 1.4) and Reading Ease 51.1 (SD 7.5), exceeding the AMA sixth-grade recommendation.
links.quote: The baseline readability analysis of the 19 included articles revealed a mean Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of 9.5 (SD: 1.4), exceeding the AMA’s recommended sixth-grade level, and a mean Flesch Reading Ease score of 51.1 (SD: 7.5), indicating “fairly difficult” readability (Table 1 , Fig. 1 ).

links.outcome: Readability and accuracy of LLM-simplified patient education text versus original
links.effect: Reading Ease improved significantly across steps (p<0.0001), greatest at Step 1 (mean gains 14-18 points); word count fell by about 1000 words; grade level rose at Step 1 then declined; accuracy stable, no hallucinations observed.
links.quote: Reading Ease improved significantly across steps ( p < 0.0001), with the greatest improvement between the original articles and Step 1, and smaller but still significant gains from Step 1 to Step 2 (Table 3 , Fig. 2 B).

links.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of AI-generated summaries across simplification steps
links.effect: Across all LLMs, grade level initially worsened at Step 1 (mean difference −1.60 for ChatGPT, −1.63 for Gemini, −1.20 for CoPilot, p < 0.05), but decreased by Step 3 (ChatGPT diff 3.46, Gemini 1.94, CoPilot 2.35).
links.quote: Grade Level changes were significant ( p < 0.0001) across steps, but an unexpected initial increase was observed between the original articles and Step 1, with a negative mean difference indicating movement away from the AMA’s sixth-grade recommendation.
